Midwifery Internship

Midwifery internship — 4 weeks of supervised practice in antenatal, labour, delivery, postnatal and newborn care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the objectives of a midwifery internship
  • Conduct antenatal and intrapartum care
  • Give postnatal and newborn care
  • Identify emergencies and refer

In simple words

The midwifery internship trains the student to care for mothers during pregnancy, labour, birth and after, and for their newborns, under supervision.

Objectives

  • Apply nursing process to antenatal, labour and postnatal mothers
  • Take a booking history and perform antenatal examination
  • Monitor labour, use the partograph and assist deliveries
  • Give care to the mother after birth and to the newborn
  • Support breastfeeding and teach the mother
  • Identify danger signs and refer urgently
  • Maintain midwifery records and reports

Skills practised

  • Booking history and antenatal examination
  • Fundal height, fetal heart and danger sign assessment
  • Support and preparation of the mother in labour
  • Monitoring contractions, cervical dilatation and fetal heart; using the partograph
  • Conducting a normal delivery under supervision
  • Care of the placenta, active management of third stage
  • Immediate newborn care: warmth, cord, vitamin K, APGAR
  • Postnatal observation of mother and baby, breastfeeding support
  • Contraception counselling and postnatal visits

🔴 Always escalate abnormal labour

Signs such as non-descent, constant pain, fetal distress or heavy bleeding need urgent obstetric referral. A student never manages an emergency alone — call, prepare, support and document.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Midwifery internship covers antenatal, labour and postnatal care plus newborn care.
  2. Labour is monitored with the partograph and fetal heart.
  3. Active management of the third stage prevents postpartum haemorrhage.
  4. Newborn care: warmth, cord, vitamin K and breastfeeding within one hour.
  5. APH, PPH, eclampsia and cord prolapse are emergencies.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Postnatal visits at day 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 days.
  2. Breastfeeding support needs correct attachment and frequent feeds.
  3. Contraception counselling starts at discharge.
  4. Records, registers and reports must be complete and accurate.
  5. Confidentiality and respect of the mother are essential.

📌 Memory trick

Midwifery internship: A-L-P — Antenatal, Labour, Postnatal.

60-second revision

  • Antenatal: booking, examination, screening, counselling.
  • Labour: monitoring, partograph, assisted delivery, placenta.
  • Newborn: warmth, cord, vitamin K, breastfeeding within one hour.
  • Postnatal: mother and baby checks, danger signs, planning.
  • Emergencies: APH, PPH, eclampsia and cord prolapse.

Test yourself

The partograph is used to monitor:

Answer: B. The partograph plots cervical dilatation, descent of the head, fetal heart and contractions.

Active management of the third stage includes:

Answer: B. Active management (oxytocin, controlled traction, massage) prevents postpartum haemorrhage.

Breastfeeding should start within the first:

Answer: B. Breastfeeding within one hour of birth promotes bonding, warmth and immunity.

Painless bright red bleeding in late pregnancy suggests:

Answer: B. Painless recurrent bright red bleeding is typical of placenta praevia.

Postnatal visits after delivery are planned on days:

Answer: A. Postnatal visits are scheduled on day 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 to detect problems early.
